title: Daily Workout · November 10
note: Tuesday · approximately 34-minute low-impact recovery session. Recent recurrent pinpoint right-sided lumbar pain with right heel-strike loading after Sunday golf and yardwork: no jogging, impact intervals, loaded twisting, or painful spinal extension. Only perform movements that are comfortable; stop if sharp pain occurs. No actual completed sets or Oura readiness score assumed. Plow pose with feet suspended is omitted today due to current lumbar symptoms; its reference-only image is not an exact demonstration. Seek assessment for recurring focal pain; urgent evaluation for new weakness, saddle numbness, or bowel/bladder changes.

items.name: Single lean-back quad stretch
items.detail: 1 min · gently alternate sides within the minute
items.instructions: Seated on floor, one leg straight, other foot beside buttock; lean back with arm support only if comfortable. Skip if it provokes lumbar or knee pain. Use existing StretchCoach image registry entry.

items.name: Butterfly stretch
items.instructions: Soles together, sit upright, do not force knees down. One 60-second hold, not separate left/right holds.

items.name: Gentle supported breathing
items.instructions: Sit or lie comfortably with spine supported; avoid twisting or extension.

items.name: Easy warm-up
items.instructions: Walk only if no sharp pain on right heel strike.

items.name: Comfortable walk
items.instructions: No jogging or incline. Keep stride comfortable; stop if focal pain appears.

items.name: Cool-down
items.instructions: Gradually slow down; do not push through pain.

items.name: Dumbbell bench press
items.instructions: Flat bench, feet supported on floor. Light manageable weight; avoid arching back or breath-holding. Skip if painful.

items.name: Supported dumbbell rows
items.instructions: Keep chest supported and lumbar spine neutral; avoid trunk rotation. Skip if painful.

items.name: Dumbbell biceps curls
items.instructions: Light-to-moderate weight; stand or sit supported, no swinging or back extension.
